r0-context.title: Load baseline context
r0-context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-crew.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas if present: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, plus the handoff, the diff, and the relevant packet. Record pass when loaded.

r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: All four close criteria met: four independently-callable, independently-tested check functions (check_engine_runnable via sys.executable distinguishes interpreter-missing/pytest-missing/working; check_work_area_present checks .git dir-or-file; check_skills_installed checks CORPUS.json + expected skill folders; check_hooks_shippable + is_git_tracked distinguishes project git-tracked vs user WIRED-only). CLI (--check-readiness) reports and refuses nonzero with named reasons, exits 0 only when all ready, never writes settings.json (verified by code read and reproduced test). Reproduced 25/25 readiness tests and 132/132 full-file tests passing.

r2-scope.title: Scope drift
r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect specific exclusions? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r2-scope.finding: Diff touches exactly scripts/install_constellation.py and tests/test_install_constellation.py (git diff --name-only confirmed). checklist_engine.py and test_checklist_engine.py, the specific exclusions, do not appear anywhere in the diff. No docs/agents/* or README.md edits despite the implementer noting a README gap -- correctly logged as out_of_scope_observations rather than acted on.

r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Reproduced independently, not restated from the implementer's claim: 'python -m pytest tests/test_install_constellation.py -k readiness -q' -> 25 passed, 107 deselected (deselected count differs from implementer's 1869 only because implementer ran against tests/ whole-directory, not the single file the handoff's Required Evidence names; same 25 passed either way). 'python -m pytest tests/test_install_constellation.py -q' -> 132 passed, 380 subtests passed. git check-ignore on both files exits 1 (tracked). Mutation-tested the load-bearing discrimination case myself: patched a fresh load_installer() module instance's check_engine_runnable to always report ready=True, re-ran test_check_engine_runnable_not_ready_when_pytest_missing against that mutated instance, and it FAILED (AssertionError: True is not false) -- the test can genuinely catch a regression, not a check that cannot fail. Read (not just grepped) every new function; settings.json is written at exactly one place in the whole file (wire_hooks(), line ~912), reached only from args.wire_hooks branches in main(), and the --check-readiness branch returns before reaching that code and explicitly raises InstallError if --wire-hooks or --baseline-only is combined with it.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: CREW_CONTEXT.md rules honored: uses sys.executable / python, never a bare 'py'/'python' string. No file writes in the new code (read-only checks), so the UTF-8/newline-on-write rule is N/A. Beyond the unit tests, ran the CLI itself end-to-end against a genuinely fresh, never-installed target (git-init'd empty temp dir as project, never-installed temp dest) -- it printed named per-item NOT READY reasons for skills/hooks and exited 1, and separately READY for a real .git-bearing project -- real evidence the refusal is not just a synthetic-test artifact (Map Anchors' Pre-Ruling 3 concern: nothing in the code path looks like it could fail to refuse on a real fresh clone; I did not run the actual g1-integrate fresh-clone check, that remains its job). Pre-Ruling 2 (settings.json never touched) verified by code read: the only settings_path.write_text call in the file lives inside wire_hooks(), unreachable from the --check-readiness branch, which explicitly rejects --wire-hooks/--baseline-only combinations before any check runs.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: No architecture reconciliation needed: additive-only change inside the existing install_constellation.py script (Pre-Ruling 4: no new script), reuses existing symbols (AGENT_TARGETS, resolve_target_roots, CORPUS_MARKER, detect_hook_wiring/describe_hook_wiring, settings_path_for_target_root) rather than re-deriving them. Repo is DEGRADED-NO-MAP per handoff so there is no structural map to diverge from. One real out-of-scope gap flagged as triage candidate tc1: README.md's Install section documents --wire-hooks/--baseline-only but not the new --check-readiness flag; correctly left untouched since README.md was not in this gate's Allowed Scope.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards -- an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.
